compiled_state.description:
Store the baseline in the projection the live comparison already computes: `description` as
`normalize_rich_text(raw)`, and `status`/`priority` as the Jira field's `name` string (for
example, `"In Progress"` and `"High"`, never local-mapped values such as `"in_progress"` or `1`).
Expected reduction is approximately 66% on the measured 18,257,550-byte predecessor file.
Measured-facts trail: session_log **1cb6-d553-6565-49b4**; do not re-derive it.

## Why this is safe without a comparator change

`outbound_field_diff.py:188,197` canonicalize the remote and baseline sides through
`inbound_mapper.map_remote_to_local` (the docstring at `:183` says storage stays vendor-shaped and
mapping happens at read time). `normalize_rich_text` converts an ADF dict through `adf_to_text` and
passes a string through unchanged. For priority/status, `map_remote_to_local` extracts the Jira
`name` through `_extract_jira_field_value`, then keys `_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_PRIORITY` or
`_JIRA_TO_LOCAL_STATUS` on that exact name; status also honors a `rebar-status:` label branch, which
is absent from baselines. Therefore exact Jira-name scalars such as `"High"` and `"In Progress"`
and their vendor dicts reach the same live comparison values. The pre-A3 reader also accepts the scalar form, which is the rollback seam.

An earlier plan incorrectly cited `_extract_jira_field`/`_diff_fields`; they have no production
callers. All behavioral oracles below cross the live `compute_update_fields` path instead.

## Why assignee is excluded

`_assignee_candidates` in `outbound_field_diff.py` builds a candidate set from the scalar plus every
non-None identity form, and `_suppressed_by_inbound` routes assignee through `_assignee_matches`.
Collapsing the vendor dict to one string would remove identity forms and could make local-wins
overwrite a concurrent remote assignee edit. The implementation must preserve the assignee value,
presence bit, and dict/scalar/null shape exactly.

## Implementation steps and exact oracles

1. In `inbound_fields.py`, add one projection helper used only by baseline writes. It returns
   `normalize_rich_text(value)` for `description`; the exact Jira `name` string for
   `status` and `priority`; and the input unchanged for every other field. It is idempotent for
   already-scalar values and preserves field absence.
2. In `BindingStore.set_baseline`, retain the existing mirrored-field allowlist and write-when-equal
   guard, but project each present field through that helper before equality comparison and storage.
   Do not project `summary` or `assignee`, and do not add a migration pass or comparator change.
3. Happy-path unit oracle:
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py::test_set_baseline_normalizes_vendor_text_shapes_but_keeps_assignee_raw`
   writes an ADF description plus Jira status/priority dicts through a real `BindingStore` and
   asserts the exact persisted baseline is description `"hello baseline"`, priority `"High"`,
   status `"In Progress"`, with the complete three-identity assignee dict unchanged.
4. Held-out live-comparison oracle:
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py` creates two real
   `BindingStore` instances, one from ADF/Jira dict values and one from their scalar equivalents.
   It calls `compute_update_fields` with the real `JiraBackend` inbound/outbound mappers and asserts
   both exact results are `{}` and the stored baselines are equal. The same file parameterizes
   exactly three local assignee identities (`ada@example.test`, `acct-ada`, `Ada Lovelace`); for
   each, Jira carries a different assignee and the oracle asserts no outbound field is emitted and
   the complete baseline assignee dict remains unchanged. A partial-input case asserts idempotence
   and that absent summary/assignee fields remain absent.
5. Stateful integration oracle:
   `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_normalization.py` initializes a real temporary
   git repository, binds one Jira key, and runs `_advance_baselines` with ADF/Jira-shaped data. It
   asserts the exact serialized baseline contains scalar description/status/priority and the raw
   assignee dict. It commits that state, runs the same production seam with scalar equivalents, and
   asserts byte-identical `bindings.json` plus a clean git worktree. Production imports remain
   inside the test function so full-suite collection first establishes the unit test package's
   shared namespace; the collect-only command below guards this order-dependent contract.
6. The existing inbound-adopt test in
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py` asserts that the dynamic baseline
   seeding caller persists exact Jira name strings and preserves raw assignee data.
7. Repository corpus oracle:
   `scripts/measure_baseline_normalization.py` loads every baseline from the named tickets ref and
   obtains local tickets through `rebar.reduce_all_tickets`. For each local id, **mutation outcome**
   is the exact JSON-comparable object `{fields, conflicts, dropped}` returned by the live
   `compute_update_fields` path and its sinks. **Mutation delta** is the count of local ids for which
   that complete object differs between the raw-baseline store and the normalized-baseline store;
   success requires a count of zero, not a similarity score or manual inspection. The forward run
   uses current code. The rollback run exports the named pre-A3 revision with `git archive` and runs
   its code in a separate subprocess with that revision first on `PYTHONPATH`, preventing module
   cache aliasing. The command exits nonzero unless every stored baseline is compared, both delta
   counts are zero, missing/error counts are zero, assignee deltas are zero, and serialized bytes
   fall by at least 50%.

## Testing

Run from this isolated A3 worktree with its `.venv` first on `PATH`:

```sh
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py \
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py \
  tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_normalization.py

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -m "not integration and not external" -q --collect-only

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/measure_baseline_normalization.py \
  --store-ref da937e47068898ed3fc6feae09acdfea963e1dd3 \
  --pre-a3-ref 550442ae58864f6f32b76ba78172251ba3119bb8

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python scripts/gen_env_registry.py --check
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest -q \
  tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py::test_generators_not_stale_and_include_new_keys \
  tests/unit/test_gen_env_registry.py::test_check_mode_clean_against_committed_tree

env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck
env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make test
```

The pinned corpus command must report 1,774/1,774 baselines compared, zero forward mutation
deltas, zero rollback mutation deltas, zero missing/errors, zero assignee deltas, and at least 50%
size reduction. Repeat with `--store-ref origin/tickets` immediately before review upload to detect
new incompatible rows. `docs/experiments/bridge-state-baseline-normalization.md` records the pinned
inputs, exact result, test contract card, and reproduction command.

## Rollback and stop conditions

- Before merge, any held-out failure, corpus delta, missing/error row, assignee delta, size reduction
  below 50%, collection failure, or repository gate failure blocks upload/merge. Production remains
  unchanged.
- After merge, an unexpected production mutation verdict or reconcile error is attributable to A3
  only after the same input succeeds under the parent of the A3 merge and fails under the A3 merge.
  On that contrast, disable both reconcile workflows immediately and poll until no run is active.
  Keep them disabled while rollback is reviewed; do not attempt a live data rewrite.
- Create a Gerrit revert of the single A3 change from a fresh worktree, retain the A3 ticket trailer
  and DCO sign-off, and do not submit until `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved comment.
  If the revert cannot clear those gates, reconciliation stays disabled and the incident remains
  operator-visible; do not bypass either gate.
- Before re-enabling, run the committed A3 corpus harness against the then-current `origin/tickets`
  with `--pre-a3-ref` set to the parent of the A3 merge and require zero rollback mutation deltas,
  zero missing/errors, and zero assignee deltas. Then require one successful reconcile workflow run
  at a SHA descending from the revert merge. Existing scalar rows remain; the pre-A3 reader accepts
  both scalar and vendor dicts, so no lossy denormalization or backup restore is attempted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] [code-verifiable] The dict-shaped baseline and scalar equivalent produce the exact same live
      `compute_update_fields` verdict through real Jira mappers. Prove with the held-out test file
      and focused pytest command above.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] All three assignee identity forms (email, accountId, displayName) preserve
      inbound-direction suppression and the raw baseline assignee dict. Prove with the three-case
      parameterization in the held-out test file.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] One real baseline-advance pass stores scalar description/status/priority,
      exactly `"In Progress"` and `"High"`, while assignee remains a dict; an equivalent second pass
      is byte-stable and leaves git clean. Prove with the integration test above.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The pinned full-corpus command reports zero forward mutation deltas as
      operationally defined above, complete coverage, and no errors.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The same command reports zero rollback mutation deltas under separately
      exported pre-A3 code, proving the old reader accepts the normalized store.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The corpus command reports at least 50% serialized-size reduction and zero
      assignee shape/value deltas.

## Files

`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/binding_store.py`,
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_fields.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_baseline.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_apply_inbound_adopt.py`,
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_baseline_normalization_heldout.py`,
`tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_baseline_normalization.py`,
`scripts/measure_baseline_normalization.py`, and
`docs/experiments/bridge-state-baseline-normalization.md`, and
`docs/env-vars.md` (mechanically regenerated registry after binding_store.py line shifts).

Scope: S-M. Depends on closed A2-1 ticket `9594-1f1c-bcd1-4774` only for sequencing and the
already-landed committed-format state; A3 consumes no new A2-1 symbol.
